## classification
ad-hoc (the node's own ad-hoc posture, no -o runtime): Cranelift WORKS under the pod profile; no allow-jit, no Seatbelt deny.
  amfid logs 'not valid ... -423 adhoc signed or signed by an unknown certificate' for every pulled binary; it is advisory, exec proceeds.
-o runtime (throwaway self-signed identity, no entitlements): Cranelift is KILLED, exit 137, SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid),
  namespace CODESIGNING indicator 'Invalid Page', fault at the first JIT page (r-x/rwx, Untagged) from wasmtime Func::call.
  Class: AMFI / hardened runtime (kernel code-signing enforcement), NOT Seatbelt (no deny line), NOT an engine error (no wasmtime error returned).
  The same kill happens unconfined on the host (crash reports under ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/wasmspike-rt-*), so the profile is not the cause.
  Pulley (Config.SetTarget("pulley64"), engine.IsPulley()=true) WORKS for the hardened variant: fib(27) correct, run ~12x slower than Cranelift here.
  Side effect seen: the hardened variant runs with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES stripped (dyld_insert=""), so it loses the path-rebase and DNS shims.
  The node did not re-sign it on pull: it was already valid, so the hardened flag survived into the pod (CS_RUNTIME=true).
